newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castorseed futures slip, palm oil rises.
newsitem.headline: Indian castorseed futures slip, palm oil rises.

text.p: Castorseed June delivery continued to lose on Thursday, falling to 1,149/1,150 rupees from 1,160/1,161 rupees per quintal on fresh speculative selling, traders said.
"Sluggish overseas demand and rising arrivals at the producing centres prompted fresh bear selling," said a dealer.
Arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region rose today to 60,000 bags (75 kg each) from 45,000 bags reported on Tuesday.
The market was closed on Wednesday for Hindu festival.
"Sentiment was weak but technically now market is oversold and short covering may help prices to bounce back from the current level," one operator added.
Groundnut oil moved up from 357/358 rupees to 367/368 rupees per 10 kg on limited arrivals of 40/50 tonnes and a shortage of ready stock which triggered panic buying.
Delivery after a week was quoted lower at 365 rupees per 10 kg.

Imported palm oil also jumped up by 10 rupees at 294/295 rupees per 10 kg on acute shortage of ready stock but delivery after a week was quoted lower at 289/290 rupees per 10 kg as traders were expecting arrivals of two vessels carrying imported palm oil at Bombay port next week, one broker said.
In Rajkot spot groundnut oil moved up from 540/545 rupees to 555 rupees per 15 kg.
The Bombay Oils and Oilseeds (ready and forward) markets will be closed on Friday for a Moslem festival.
